summary: Tested 3 things: owner admin login, admin staying Greek with EN on, and static public content in both languages. Backend: 5/5 pytest pass. Both owner accounts (manoliszografakis@gmail.com, apostolakisalex@gmail.com / matestzografakis_11.11) log in with role=admin and reach /api/admin/workspace and /api/admin/pending. Login works with an uppercase email. A wrong password gives 401. Frontend (390x844, languagePreference=en): both owners logged in through the UI and landed on /admin. I scanned the DOM for Latin-only text in the overview and all 11 sections (Μέλη + member detail, Ημερολόγιο, Φωτογραφίες, Εγγραφές, Περιεχόμενο, Τμήματα, Φόρμες, Ιστορικό, Αξιολογήσεις, Πρόοδος, Παρουσίες). The overview and sections render Greek, including the Shell footer 'Χανιά · Αθήνα · Online', the bottom tabs (Αρχική/Ηχοθεραπεία/Εκπαιδευτικά/Εκδηλώσεις/Προφίλ), Πρόοδος staff, the MemberProfile staff detail and Αξιολογήσεις. The non-admin 'Περιορισμένη πρόσβαση' screen is Greek too. The only Latin text was user data, CMS data, raw enum chips and one hard-coded English 'Upload' button in ResourcesSection. With EN on, /treatments, /treatment/{sound-bath,ihomasaz,breathwork} and /service/{ergastiria-omilies,xenodocheia-spa,etairikes-ekdiloseis} render fully in English (titles, taglines, intro, DURATION/FORMAT/EXPERIENCE labels, body). The home Services grid shows English tiles and the founder card reads 'Manolis Zografakis'. Toggling back to EL shows Greek. Regression: home, soundhealing, training, levels, events and the member tabs switch to EN, and CMS seminar and blog text stays in its authored Greek. One gap remains: the level titles on member /academy are Greek-only static backend constants.

minor.issue: Level titles and descriptions come from the hard-coded LEVELS constant in backend/school.py:12-17 and are Greek only. They are static app copy, not CMS content, so member /academy shows 'Τα θεμέλια της πρακτικής', 'Εμβάθυνση στην ατομική πρακτική', 'Ομαδικά Sound Baths', 'Επαγγελματική εκπαίδευση' and their descriptions in Greek when EN is on.

ui_bugs.issue: Admin-only English text despite ForceGreekLanguage: the 'Upload' button label (ResourcesSection.tsx:~261) and the Alert strings 'File too large'/'Max 12 MB per file.', 'Uploaded', 'Upload failed', 'Try again', 'Resource locked', 'Open failed', 'Remove resource?', 'Delete', 'Cancel', 'Delete failed' (ResourcesSection.tsx ~110-215). The admin area must always be Greek.
With EN on, the L1-L4 level titles and descriptions from /school/catalog stay Greek. Map them by level id to bilingual frontend strings, or return el/en fields from the backend.

issues: Inside admin, the globe language-toggle still shows 'EN' but does nothing, because ForceGreekLanguage sets toggle to a no-op. Either hide it in admin or let it change the global preference (affecting public pages only) and give feedback, so admins are not confused.
The Τύπος and Δημόσια ενότητα chips show raw enum values (page, lesson, announcement, site_settings, home, services ...). Greek labels already exist in the helper text; consider Greek chip labels.
Ιστορικό shows raw action keys (member.level_verify, calendar.create, media.upload) and raw UUID entity ids. These should be Greek labels.
The back link is '← Treatments' in both languages (TreatmentDetail.tsx:34). The same goes for the TreatmentsOverview title and <title>. This may be intended branding; confirm with the owner.

action_items: Translate the admin-only strings in ResourcesSection.tsx to Greek: the 'Upload' button and all Alert.alert titles, messages and button texts. Use t() so the forced-Greek context applies, or hard-code Greek since this branch is admin-only.
Make the static level catalogue (backend/school.py LEVELS, shown via /school/catalog on member /academy) bilingual, e.g. a frontend map by level id using t().
Optional UX: hide the language-toggle in the admin workspace, or make it work, since it currently shows 'EN' and is a no-op.
Optional: show Greek labels instead of raw enum and action keys in the admin Περιεχόμενο chips and Ιστορικό list.
critical_code_review_comments: seed_admins.py keeps the shared owner password in plain text in source control (ADMIN_SEED_PASSWORD). This is per the owner's request, but consider moving it to an env var.

seed_admins uses $set role=admin on any existing user with those emails and writes password_hash only on insert. If one of these emails had registered earlier with a different password, it becomes admin and keeps the old password, not the shared one. That does not apply today, since both logins work.
ForceGreekLanguage overrides the Language context correctly, and Shell and BottomNavigation are inside it, so the footer and tabs are Greek.

success_rate.frontend: ~93%: all requested flows pass; 2 remaining bilingual gaps (ResourcesSection admin English strings, academy level titles Greek in EN)

seed_data_creation: None created. Used the existing owner admin accounts and uitest_167043@test.gr (read-only browsing).

rca_of_issue: ResourcesSection was written with hard-coded English for the admin upload controls and Alerts, so ForceGreekLanguage cannot affect them. Academy level titles come from a backend constant with no language variant.
